subject.title: Multi-profile profile targeting/config truth is ambiguous with ~/.openclaw-* homes on macOS

question: What should explicit root --profile mean when it conflicts with inherited state/config environment, inherited LaunchAgent identity, profile-name casing, or separate ~/.openclaw-* homes on macOS?
rationale: Source inspection confirms overlapping precedence paths, but changing them affects supported operator layouts and compatibility for intentional custom service-label or env overrides.

options.title: Make explicit profile authoritative
options.body: Treat root --profile as the selected config/state/service target, clear only stale OpenClaw-managed service identity, preserve intentional custom labels, and make status/restart show the resolved boundary.

options.title: Preserve env/label override precedence
options.body: Document that inherited OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR, OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH, and OPENCLAW_LAUNCHD_LABEL can override --profile and require operators to clear them for cross-profile commands.

options.title: Keep as broader design umbrella
options.body: Defer code repair until maintainers decide casing, mixed-home support, service identity, config/load truth, and host-surface proof together.

recommendation.title: Make explicit profile authoritative
recommendation.body: Treat root --profile as the selected config/state/service target, clear only stale OpenClaw-managed service identity, preserve intentional custom labels, and make status/restart show the resolved boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history and current blame both point most strongly to steipete for the profile and launchd operator contract.
